practices.label: Least privilege
practices.definition: Every account, role and agent holds only the rights its task needs, and nothing it might need later.

practices.label: Defence in depth
practices.definition: More than one control stands between an attacker and the asset, so one failure is not a breach.

practices.label: Default deny
practices.definition: Nothing passes a boundary unless a rule allows it; the allow list is the policy.

practices.label: Network segmentation
practices.definition: Zones with distinct trust levels are separated, and the flows between them are named and limited.

practices.label: Zero trust access
practices.definition: No request is trusted for where it comes from; identity, device and context decide every access.

practices.label: Multi-factor authentication
practices.definition: Every console and privileged login asks for a second factor; a password alone is refused.

practices.label: Federated identity
practices.definition: Applications trust one identity provider over SAML or OIDC instead of keeping their own passwords.

practices.label: Secrets in a store
practices.definition: Keys and passwords live in a secret store and never in a prompt, a repository or a config file.

practices.label: Machine identity register
practices.definition: Every service account, key and certificate has an owner and a rotation date in one register.

practices.label: Separation of duties
practices.definition: The person who requests, the person who approves and the person who applies a change are not the same.

practices.label: Periodic access review
practices.definition: Accounts and rights are reviewed on a schedule; orphans are disabled and the review is recorded.

practices.label: Joiner and leaver process
practices.definition: Access is granted on a documented request and removed within a stated time of leaving.

practices.label: Encryption in transit
practices.definition: Traffic crosses a boundary only over approved TLS versions, and the weak ones are refused.

practices.label: Key rotation
practices.definition: Keys and certificates have an owner and a rotation date, and a rotation is recorded when it happens.

practices.label: Hash evidence at capture
practices.definition: Every artifact is hashed when it is saved and the digest is recorded, so later copies can be checked.

practices.label: Authorised testing only
practices.definition: Scanning and attacks happen inside a signed scope and rules of engagement, against the pod the team owns.

practices.label: Agreed scope and terms
practices.definition: The work starts from a written agreement: what is in scope, what is out, and who signs.

practices.label: Passive before active
practices.definition: Open sources and passive lookups come before any packet reaches the target.

practices.label: Retest to closure
practices.definition: A finding is closed only by a retest that shows the fix, and every finding ends Closed, Open or Risk accepted.

practices.label: CVSS severity
practices.definition: Each finding carries a CVSS score, so severity is a number that can be ranked and defended.

practices.label: Likelihood-times-impact scoring
practices.definition: Each risk is scored on a stated scale for likelihood and impact, and the score decides the order.

practices.label: Threat modelling
practices.definition: Threats are enumerated per component with a method, and each is tied to a control or an accepted risk.

practices.label: Compensating controls
practices.definition: Where a control cannot be applied, another control covering the same risk is named and justified.

practices.label: Tabletop exercise
practices.definition: The team walks through an incident on paper with injects, and the after-action report names improvements.

practices.label: Backup before change
practices.definition: A configuration is copied before it is edited, so the change can be reversed in one step.

practices.label: Change control
practices.definition: Every change is requested, reviewed, reversible and recorded before it reaches a system.

practices.label: Rollback plan
practices.definition: A change carries the steps that undo it, written before it is made.

practices.label: Managed patching
practices.definition: Updates are inventoried, prioritised, tested, applied and verified on a cadence, not when something breaks.

practices.label: Hardening baseline
practices.definition: Hosts are configured to a written benchmark and checked against it, so drift from the baseline is visible.

practices.label: Configuration scanning
practices.definition: Hosts are scanned against a benchmark on a schedule, and the failed checks become findings.

practices.label: Configuration record
practices.definition: Every device configuration is saved, versioned and compared after a change.

practices.label: Build record
practices.definition: A build is recorded step by step with firmware, versions and settings as it is made.

practices.label: Media sanitisation
practices.definition: Storage is cleared, purged or destroyed to the written level before it leaves, and the action is recorded.

practices.label: Infrastructure as code
practices.definition: Resources are declared in versioned templates and deployed from them, not clicked into being.

practices.label: Drift detection
practices.definition: The running environment is compared with its template and any difference is treated as a finding.

practices.label: Rebuild, do not repair
practices.definition: A compromised or drifted system is replaced from a known-good image rather than patched in place.

practices.label: Reproducible builds
practices.definition: A system or a test suite can be rebuilt from its record and produce the same result.

practices.label: Blue-green deployment
practices.definition: Two identical environments take turns serving traffic, so a release switches over and can switch back.

practices.label: Canary release
practices.definition: A change reaches a small share of traffic first and is watched before it reaches everyone.

practices.label: Automated rollback
practices.definition: A release that fails its health check is reverted by the pipeline without a person deciding.

practices.label: Pipeline gates
practices.definition: A build cannot proceed past a scan, a test or an approval that failed; a gate that blocks is a control.

practices.label: Dependency and image scanning
practices.definition: Third-party packages and container images are scanned for known vulnerabilities before release.

practices.label: Secret scanning
practices.definition: Repositories and prompts are scanned for credentials, and a finding blocks the build.

practices.label: Software bill of materials
practices.definition: A release lists its components (CycloneDX or SPDX), so a vulnerable dependency can be found.

practices.label: Guardrail regression tests
practices.definition: Every blocked attack case becomes a test the pipeline runs, so a removed guardrail fails the build.

practices.label: Policy as code
practices.definition: Guardrails are written as rules the platform enforces, so a non-compliant resource is denied or flagged.

practices.label: Interface contract
practices.definition: Endpoints, requests and responses are specified before they are built, and the build is checked against the spec.

practices.label: Naming and tagging
practices.definition: Every resource carries the agreed name and tags, so cost, ownership and environment can be read from it.

practices.label: Budget guardrails
practices.definition: A budget with alerts is set before the first resource, and the alert is tested.

practices.label: Tear down after use
practices.definition: Billable resources are stopped or deleted in the same task that created them, and the record says so.

practices.label: Right-sizing
practices.definition: Resources are sized from measured use, reviewed and shrunk when the measurement says so.

practices.label: Multi-zone redundancy
practices.definition: Services run across availability zones so the loss of one zone does not stop them.

practices.label: Health checks
practices.definition: A load balancer or scaler routes only to instances that answer a health probe, and replaces the ones that do not.

practices.label: Backups tested by restore
practices.definition: A backup counts only after a restore from it has been performed and its hashes compared.

practices.label: Recovery objectives
practices.definition: Recovery time and recovery point targets are written per service, and a drill is timed against them.

practices.label: Centralised logging
practices.definition: Every host ships its logs to one place where they are kept, searched and alerted on.

practices.label: Capture a baseline
practices.definition: Normal traffic and logs are captured before an attack, so the attack can be told from normal.

practices.label: Alert to ticket
practices.definition: A detection opens a ticket with an owner and a due time, so nothing fires into silence.

practices.label: Detection as code
practices.definition: Detections are written as versioned rules, mapped to a technique id and validated against a test attack.

practices.label: ATT&CK-mapped reporting
practices.definition: Findings, indicators and detections carry the technique id, so they can be compared across teams.

practices.label: Indicators from evidence
practices.definition: Indicators are extracted from alerts and packets, each traceable to its source and technique.

practices.label: Contain before analysing
practices.definition: An active attacker is blocked and the block is timestamped before the deeper analysis begins.

practices.label: Evidence-backed timeline
practices.definition: Every row of an incident timeline points at the log line or capture it came from.

practices.label: Lessons learned
practices.definition: After an incident or a drill, what worked and what did not is written down with an owner for each change.

practices.label: Written policy
practices.definition: Rules are written as shall statements with an owner, a review date and the standard they implement.

practices.label: Written runbooks
practices.definition: Routine operations are written as steps a colleague could follow, and the steps are kept current.

practices.label: Sign and version documents
practices.definition: A document carries an id, a version, an owner, a date and a status, and a change makes a new version.

practices.label: As-built documentation
practices.definition: What was actually built is recorded, with addresses, versions and owners, and handed over with the system.

practices.label: Architecture decision records
practices.definition: Each significant design choice is recorded with its context, options and consequences.

practices.label: Requirements before design
practices.definition: The design starts from written requirements and constraints, and each design element traces to one.

practices.label: Addressing plan
practices.definition: Subnets, addresses and names are planned on paper before any device is configured.

practices.label: Test and acceptance
practices.definition: A build is accepted against written tests with recorded results, not against a feeling that it works.

practices.label: Structured troubleshooting
practices.definition: Identify the problem, establish a theory, test it, plan and act, verify, document: in that order.

practices.label: Asset inventory
practices.definition: Every asset is listed with an owner, a location and a classification before it is protected.

practices.label: Data classification
practices.definition: Information is classified on a written scale, and handling rules follow the class.

practices.label: Personal data discovery
practices.definition: Stores are scanned for personal data before and after a clean-up, and the counts are recorded.

practices.label: Control mapping
practices.definition: Each control is mapped to the criteria it satisfies across frameworks, with an owner and an evidence source.

practices.label: Evidence by design
practices.definition: Every control names the evidence that proves it operates, and the evidence is collected as the work happens.

practices.label: Corrective action
practices.definition: Every nonconformity gets a cause, a corrective action, an owner and a date, and the action is checked.

practices.label: Supplier tiering
practices.definition: Suppliers are tiered by the access and data they hold, and the top tier carries written terms.

practices.label: Write for leadership
practices.definition: A report opens with what a non-technical reader must decide, and the technical detail follows.

practices.label: Metrics with targets
practices.definition: Each metric has a formula, a source and a target, so a number can be read as good or bad.

practices.label: Customer assurance
practices.definition: A customer question is answered with evidence or an honest gap, never with a promise.

practices.label: Input and output guardrails
practices.definition: Prompts and model outputs pass through filters that block or contain the listed attack cases.

practices.label: Least privilege for agents
practices.definition: An agent or tool call holds a scoped credential and no admin right, and its actions are logged.

practices.label: Redact before write
practices.definition: Personal data is detected and removed before a prompt, a log or a dataset is stored.

practices.label: Model file scanning
practices.definition: Serialised models are scanned for unsafe code before they are loaded, and the result is recorded.

practices.label: Human checkpoint
practices.definition: AI-assisted work passes a named human check before it is acted on, and the check is recorded.

practices.label: Model cards
practices.definition: Every model in use has a card: purpose, data, limits, owner and evaluation results.

practices.label: Shadow AI discovery
practices.definition: Unsanctioned AI tools are found from network and usage data, and each gets a decision.

practices.label: Suites with a pass line
practices.definition: An attack or evaluation suite states what passing means before it runs.

practices.label: Work tracked on a board
practices.definition: Every task of the week is a card with an owner and a state on the team board.

practices.label: Encryption at rest
practices.definition: Stored data, snapshots and backups are encrypted under a managed key, and nothing is shared or public.

practices.label: Decouple with queues
practices.definition: Producers and consumers talk through a queue with a dead-letter queue, so a slow consumer loses nothing.

practices.label: Redundant paths
practices.definition: A second link or device exists for every single point of failure, and the failover is tested by pulling the cable.

practices.label: Idempotent automation
practices.definition: Running the automation twice changes nothing the second time, which is how a run is known to be complete.
